# PLAN — iteration 5
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 0.329 ns register-to-register WNS and 0.076 ns hold slack, so iteration 5 must strictly improve register-to-register slack to advance the `maximize_freq` objective. The seed stores delayed products and reduces eight 32-bit terms through a carry-save tree and final adder; prior final-adder experiments were rejected, so this plan changes the datapath structure instead.

## Hypothesis
A transposed FIR using registered partial sums should replace the wide output reduction with shorter per-stage constant-multiply-and-add paths, improving routed register-to-register slack while retaining one-sample-per-cycle throughput.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the `prod[0:63]` product-delay chains and the combinational carry-save reduction with a transposed FIR: keep a signed 16-bit input sample register, seven signed 32-bit partial-sum registers, and the registered `y_out`. On each clock, compute `y_out` from the previous sample and first partial sum, and update each partial sum from that same previous sample, its coefficient, and the next partial sum; use 32-bit modular arithmetic so arbitrary signed parameter values retain the existing product and sum semantics. Reset every state register and `y_out` to zero, preserve the interface and `// @latency 1`, and ensure the output still uses the previous cycle’s sample.
